value.snippet: Video: 00:07:47 What a difference a year makes! Today Hera’s asteroid mission for planetary defence is cruising through deep space on the far side of the Sun, headed to its final destination: the Didymos binary asteroid system. But a year ago, on 7 October 2024, it was unsure if the mission was ever going to take off at all. Its launcher was grounded due to a launch anomaly and Hurricane Milton was closing on Cape Canaveral! The mission needed to lift off then and there because it had to perform a flyby of Mars to speed it on its way to Didymos. Any delay would add years to its travel time. But Hera received permission for launch and the heavens cleared just half an hour before launch. Liftoff happened to plan – the team had their mission in space! value.snippet: Video: 00:00:48 On 28 September 2026, ESA’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer ( Juice ) successfully completed a gravity assist flyby of Earth. Flight controllers guided the spacecraft close to our home planet to increase its velocity by 3.5 km/s and deflect its trajectory by an angle of 20°. As Juice flew just 8640 km above the Indian Ocean, it snapped a series of images with its onboard monitoring cameras, giving us a unique ‘Juice eye view’ of our home planet. Juice’s monitoring cameras provide 1024 x 1024 pixel snapshots that can be processed in colour. Their main purpose is to monitor the spacecraft’s various booms and antennas, especially during the challenging period after launch. The photos they captured of Earth during the flyby are a bonus. Flight VV30 lifted off on 15 September at 03:21 (14 September at 22:21 local time). FLEX is designed to reveal a phenomenon invisible to the human eye: the faint fluorescence emitted by plants as they photosynthesise. Equipped with a Fluorescence Imaging Spectrometer, FLEX will detect and measure this incredibly weak signal from orbit. Because the fluorescence varies with plant health and environmental conditions, the measurements will provide scientists with new information about photosynthetic activity and vegetation stress on a global scale. value.snippet: India's rapidly growing demand for electricity could force it to add substantially more coal-fired power capacity than planned, the head of the power sector planner said on Tuesday. The South Asian nation, which planned last year to add 97 GW of coal power capacity to reach 307 GW by 2035, currently has about 230 GW of capacity.

value.title: Cobre defines staged, modular expansion plan for Sierra Atacama copper mine
value.snippet: ASX-listed copper developer Cobre has defined a fully funded, staged and modular expansion pathway for its 62%-owned Sierra Atacama project, in Chile, leveraging existing infrastructure and targeting an initial increase in copper cathode capacity to 18 000 t/y before increasing production to 25 000 t/y and further to 50 000 t/y in the long term. Stage 1 of the project will comprise restoring the site's existing capacity to 18 000 t/y, with a detailed engineering review of the existing plant having established the scope to refurbish and upgrade the operating solvent extraction circuit and recommission the currently unused second electrowinning bay.

value.title: Canadian tailings reprocessor Cerro de Pasco awarded rights to Peruvian site
value.snippet: Québec-based Cerro de Pasco Resources has been awarded through a public auction the rights to tailings held in the Quiulacocha tailings storage facility, in Peru, for economic reprocessing. The Sale Committee of Activos Mineros (AMSAC) awarded the mineral rights and surface rights over the tailings to Cerro de Pasco's subsidiary in Peru, which, once definitively executed, will enable the company to consolidate the tailings with its 100%-owned El Metalurgista concession.

value.title: Nel, Rheinmetall partners to decentralise renewable fuel production in Norway
value.snippet: Norwegian industrial gas company Nel and German defence contractor and integrated technology group Rheinmetall have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to explore joint opportunities in decentralised renewable fuel production. The collaboration will combine Nel's electrolyser technology for renewable hydrogen production with Rheinmetall's Giga PtX concept and systems-integration expertise to assess scalable, modular solutions for the localised production of low-carbon synthetic fuels for defence and critical infrastructure applications.

value.title: Australia’s New South Wales backs gas power as coal plants shut
value.snippet: Australia’s most populous State has ruled out batteries and other energy storage in its latest tender to manage expected power shortfalls when its aging coal plants close. New South Wales will seek 1 500 MW in the tender to firm up supply, most of which will be from natural gas peaking plants, State Energy Minister Penny Sharpe said at the Australian Financial Review’s Energy and Climate Summit in Sydney.

value.title: India's NTPC seeks overseas buyers for green ammonia, low-carbon fuels
value.snippet: India's top power producer NTPC is in talks with potential buyers in Japan, South Korea and Germany for green ammonia and other low-carbon fuels, chairperson Gurdeep Singh said on Tuesday. India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments.

value.title: EnergyX signs binding $2bn lithium supply deal with Trafigura
value.snippet: Lithium startup EnergyX said on Monday it has signed a $2-billion binding offtake to supply commodities trader Trafigura with the battery metal from Chile and the US, one of the largest deals ever tied to direct lithium extraction technology. The 10-year agreement, which Reuters ​is first to report, comes as strong demand for lithium from the fast-growing stationary battery storage system market has offset uneven sales in the global electric vehicle market, which had been the primary user of the ultralight metal for years.

value.title: France to become Eramet's top shareholder via miner's capital hike
value.snippet: France is set to become Eramet's largest shareholder by increasing its stake during a €500-million ($558.50-million) capital increase later this year, the French mining group said on Monday. Nickel, manganese and lithium producer Eramet had announced in February it would conduct a capital hike to help recover from a slump in earnings and a jump in debt.

value.snippet: Argentina's government said on Tuesday it had filed a request for provisional measures with the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea seeking to halt British-authorized hydrocarbon activity near the Falkland Islands. The request aims to prevent the United Kingdom from exploiting hydrocarbon resources on the continental shelf of the Northern Falklands Basin, the government added in a statement.

value.title: Rio Tinto on track to release $5bn in capital after stronger Q3 iron-ore sales
value.snippet: Diversified miner Rio Tinto said on Wednesday it was on track to release about $5-billion in capital by the end of 2026, after strong mine performance helped lift third-quarter iron-ore sales from its Pilbara operations above market expectations. The world's largest iron-ore producer sold 85.7-million metric tons of the steel-making commodity from Pilbara in the quarter ended September 30, up 2% from a year earlier and ahead of a Visible Alpha consensus estimate of 84.41-million tons.

value.title: Aluminium's calm belies lingering supply-chain stress, Reuters column says
value.snippet: Iranian missile attacks on Gulf smelters and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz have knocked out almost 3-million metric tons of aluminium production capacity. Yet, eight months on, the market is seemingly unconcerned. Indeed, London Metal Exchange (LME) three-month aluminium is now trading just above $3 000 a ton, which is where it was in early February before the US and Israel unleashed Operation Epic Fury against Iran.

value.title: BHP's Escondida, supervisors hold talks in bid to avert strike
value.snippet: In a last-ditch effort to avoid a strike, the supervisors' union at BHP's Escondida copper mine in Chile and company representatives are holding talks, the union said late on Tuesday. Earlier in the day, the union announced it would begin a strike on Wednesday after mediation efforts to tie up a new collective labor contract had failed.

value.title: Glencore shares trade higher on ASX debut as investors eye copper
value.snippet: Glencore's shares traded heavily in their debut on Wednesday on the Australian Securities Exchange, where the miner and trader hopes to secure a better valuation from investors seeking greater copper exposure. Glencore CEO Gary Nagle expects strong demand from Australian investors betting on copper's role in electrification, he said on Friday, as demand rises for the metal's use in power grid expansions, transport and AI data centres.

value.title: WMI seminar explores challenges to sustainably grasping opportunity-rich mining future
value.snippet: The Wits Mining Institute (WMI) held its annual industry seminar on October 8, titled “From legacy to leadership: shaping sustainable mining futures”. Wits Faculty of Engineering and the Built Environment Dean Professor Cuthbert Musingwini opened the seminar by emphasising the importance of collaboration, noting the support that the WMI received from mining groups Sibanye-Stillwater and South32 which enabled them to convene platforms that bring stakeholders together to unpack issues in the mining sector.
